description: Figure 5(b) is a line plot illustrating the ratio of training loss for several methods relative to a “Vanilla” baseline as a function of compute, showing how each method’s loss ratio changes as FLOPs increase. The x-axis is labeled “FLOPs” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning approximately from \(10^{17}\) to \(10^{19}\), with major ticks at powers of ten. The y-axis is labeled “Loss Ratio” and appears linear, ranging roughly from about 2.4 up to about 3.4 with evenly spaced tick marks (approximately 0.2 increments). Multiple colored solid lines are shown (with no visible point markers), each decreasing monotonically from left to right: the blue “Vanilla” line stays at a constant ratio of 1.0 across the entire x-range (serving as the reference), while the other method lines start near the top of the axis around \(\sim 3.3\)–3.4 at the lowest FLOPs and decline toward the lower end of the axis near \(\sim 2.4\)–2.6 by the highest FLOPs; the curves are steepest at the left (low FLOPs) and flatten progressively as FLOPs increase.
